RMabs are superior to the FDA‐approved antibodies in the detection of estrogen receptor (FMab vs RMab) and progesterone receptor expression (Dako FMab vs RMab).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rabbit monoclonal antibody is a better choice than the mouse monoclonal antibody.

we compared the performance of rabbit monoclonal antibody (RMab) and FDA-approved mouse monoclonal antibody with the FDA-approved Herceptest in breast carcinoma cell blocks using conventional microscopy and image analysis.
the use of RMab for ER, PR and Her2 detection in cell block sections using both visual and image detection methods is comparable to that of FMab.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rabbit monoclonal ER, PR, and HER2 antibodies have a higher sensitivity and a lower interobserver variation than the corresponding mouse monoclonal antibodies.
RMabs have better performance in detection of Her2 overexpression in breast carcinoma cell blocks than HercepTest.
the use of RMab in cell block sections is feasible and can be used for accurate assessment of ER, PR and Her2 status in breast carcinomas.
